solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scoundrel's behind pretentious talk in clip

indicators.note: 'is behind' places one piece after another, so the first-named part goes second

parts.note: bull is empty, pompous nonsense
a dog is a low, contemptible fellow

explanation.surface: A villain lurks behind some showy chatter in a film clip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clip' suggests a video excerpt, but it is the stationery item. The 's stands for 'is', so the scoundrel sits behind the talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulldog clip is the sprung metal grip used to hold a stack of papers, so the word alone names that clip.

clue.text: Ineffectual chap — deceptive character extracting pounds

indicators.note: extracting something means pulling it out, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: someone who bluffs pretends to more than they have
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A feeble man is described as a con artist who swindles people out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L from BLUFFER to leave BUFFER. 'Pounds' looks like the money being swindled, but it is just the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: An old buffer is British slang for a foolish, bumbling elderly man who achieves little.

clue.text: Ludicrous barrel blocking fluid haulage

indicators.note: to block is to sit in the way, so one piece lodges inside another
something fluid flows and changes shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
bl is a standard abbreviation for barrel

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the idea of a barrel getting in the way of transporting liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' looks like the liquid being hauled, but it signals the rearrangement. The barrel abbreviation lands just before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laughable deserves to be laughed at, the same as ridiculous or absurd.

clue.text: American lawyer raised challenge about a source of information

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney in the US

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something turns it to read bottom to top
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a test is a trial or challenge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A US attorney lodges an objection about an informant.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first, and then the whole challenge is turned upward, as suits a down entry; DA stays put on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A data set is a collection of records gathered for analysis, so it is somewhere facts can be drawn from.

clue.text: US soldier welcoming a coarse Italian patriot

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a GI is an American enlisted soldier
taken as written
ribald means vulgar or crude

explanation.surface: An American GI greets a crude Italian freedom fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier's two letters split to take in the rest whole. Ribald means bawdy, a near synonym of coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the military campaigns that unified Italy in the nineteenth century, a national hero.

clue.text: Historic warrior — one with a strange attitude seems initially to retreat

indicators.note: retreating means moving backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word it follows

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An old-time fighter with an odd outlook appears ready to withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: I, A, RUM and AS make IARUMAS, which retreats to give SAMURAI. 'Rum' meaning odd is old-fashioned British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary military class of feudal Japan, sword-bearing fighters of past centuries.

clue.text: Special attention for this point?

parts.note: sp is a standard abbreviation for special
to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a particular argument deserves extra focus.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a sharp point that demands special attention is the tip of a weapon, and the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long weapon whose business end is its pointed head, which anyone facing it watches carefully.

clue.text: A blemish covered by old woman's make-up

indicators.note: in a down entry, being covered by something means sitting beneath it, so that piece comes first

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a scar is a mark left on the skin
taken as written

explanation.surface: Grandma hides a spot with her cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, being covered by something puts it underneath, so the mother comes first; the setter lets the article trail the blemish. 'Old woman' is a stock phrase for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is a cosmetic brushed onto eyelashes to darken and thicken them, one kind of facial cosmetic.

clue.text: Right fuss involving one form of communication

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: to involve is to include, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A proper commotion breaks out over a way of getting a message across.
explanation.walkthrough: ADO takes in I to make ADIO, after R. 'One' looks like part of the definition but is the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio transmits voice and signals by electromagnetic waves, a means of broadcasting and messaging.

clue.text: Suggestion pub open around start of evening

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: to undo a parcel is to open it

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of evening

explanation.surface: Someone proposes that the pub open its doors as night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' reads as the pub's opening time, but it is a verb meaning unfasten, which then wraps around the evening's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect hint, usually suggestive or insinuating rather than stated outright.

clue.text: Plant with grass turned over around it, attended by bird

indicators.note: to be attended by is to have someone alongside, so one piece follows another
around means encircling, so one piece wraps another
turning something over flips it, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: turf is grass with its roots and soil
taken as written
a ree is a female ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a plant whose turf has been dug up around it, with a bird in attendance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is not the plant itself but sods of earth, flipped to go around the 'it'. The bird is the female ruff, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit tree, such as an apple or plum, is a woody plant grown for its edible crop.

clue.text: Confused answer covers this French commune

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so the letters sit concealed inside a longer run

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A muddled reply hides the name of a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' looks like an anagram signal, but nothing is rearranged: the two words simply contain the answer, and 'this' points to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedan is a town in the Ardennes department of northern France, scene of famous battles in 1870 and 1940.

clue.text: H is found in fifteen consecutive letters in code

indicators.note: being found in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: the alphabet run from E to S is exactly fifteen letters long, so read it as E TO S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle fact: the letter H falls within a run of fifteen alphabet letters in some cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true, since H lies between E and S. The trick is reading the fifteen letters as the phrase 'E to S'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the guiding set of values or moral principles of a group, much like a code of conduct.

clue.text: Lawyers about to take part in song

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
ca is short for circa, meaning about
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A group of lawyers is about to join in with a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to take part' reads as one phrase, but 'about' is the Latin abbreviation circa and 'part' is a theatrical role.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a Venetian boatmen's song, or a piece of music imitating its rocking rhythm.

clue.text: Retracts blade roughly, showing damage from conflict

indicators.note: done roughly means done carelessly, so the letters end up out of order

parts.note: all thirteen letters are used

explanation.surface: A fighter pulls back a sword clumsily after an exchange that left wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of the two opening words is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Battle-scarred describes someone or something marked by wounds or wear from past fighting or struggle.

clue.text: Snape is gutted Harry strained regarding uphill task

indicators.note: something strained is forced out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Harry

explanation.surface: A Harry Potter scene: Professor Snape is devastated, and Harry struggles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' looks like it describes Snape's mood, but it applies to Harry, leaving HY. Sisyphus was condemned to roll a boulder uphill for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisyphean describes endless, futile labour, after the Greek king forever pushing a rock up a hill.

clue.text: Sauce prepared again, essence not originally being included

indicators.note: something included is put inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: made once more

indicators.note: not originally means without the original, opening letter

parts.note: the soul is the essential core of something

explanation.surface: A cook redoes a sauce, this time leaving out the extract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essence' suggests a cooking extract, but it means the spirit or core, which loses its first letter before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Remoulade is a French mayonnaise-based condiment flavoured with herbs, capers and mustard.

clue.text: One choosing empty life in particular part of national activity

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a sector is one area of the economy, such as the public sector

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of life

explanation.surface: Someone opts for a hollow existence within one corner of public life.
explanation.walkthrough: The long phrase is a roundabout way of saying a slice of the economy. In Britain a selector is someone who picks a national sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: A selector picks people or things, especially the members of a team, so the word means a person who chooses.

clue.text: Prospective wealth he has left to marine? It's a shocking event

parts.note: elect after a title means chosen but not yet in office, as in president-elect

indicators.note: something that has left is gone, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: riches are wealth
taken as written, to be removed
taken as written
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A man has bequeathed his expected fortune to a marine, which comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: RICHES minus HE leaves RICS. 'Shocking' is a pun: an electric storm brings lightning, a literal shock.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric storm is a thunderstorm with lightning, an occurrence that delivers electrical discharges.

clue.text: Bunch in Society very much enthralled by food

indicators.note: to be enthralled is to be held captive, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: tuck is British school slang for food, especially sweets
S is the abbreviation for society
so means to a great degree

explanation.surface: A group in high society is utterly captivated by the catering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunch' looks like a group of socialites, but it is a clump of grass. Tuck is British school slang for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a dense tuft or clump of grass growing in a raised mound.

clue.text: Waterproof garment, medium type, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: oils are a painting medium
a kind is a type or sort

explanation.surface: A description of a raincoat of middling style, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a clothing size, but it is the artist's medium OILS. KIND loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a coat made of cloth treated with oil so that rain runs off it.

clue.text: Church location most suitable to house religious figure

indicators.note: to house something is to give it a home inside, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: very means exactly right, as in 'the very thing'
St is short for saint

explanation.surface: Someone seeks the best church spot to put a statue of a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most suitable' looks like a superlative, but it means precisely right, as in 'the very man for the job'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is a room in a church where vestments are kept and clergy prepare for services.

clue.text: Try to hear what happens in autumn, though not at first

indicators.note: not at first means without the opening letter

parts.note: in autumn the leaves drop from the trees

explanation.surface: Someone strains to catch the sounds of autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase LEAVES DROP loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to a private conversation, attempting to overhear it.

clue.text: French life missing one French name for poison

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: vie is the French word for life
the Roman numeral for one, to be removed
nom is the French word for name

explanation.surface: A French life lacking a French name is reduced to poison, like a sinister thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: VIE drops I to leave VE, followed by NOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is the toxic fluid injected by snakes and spiders, a natural poison.

clue.text: Rifle given popular outlaw's name

indicators.note: given means with something added, so one piece is followed by the next

parts.note: to rifle a drawer is to search it and steal
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A gun is named after a well-loved bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like a gun but is the verb meaning to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the legendary English outlaw of Sherwood Forest, so Robin is the bandit's first name.

clue.text: Scoundrel to go down after intervention by University

indicators.note: something intervening comes between, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: to go down in a contest is to be beaten
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A rogue is sent down after the university steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: U comes between the letters of LOSE. 'Go down' also hints at being sent down, expelled from a university, which is a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse, figuratively, is a contemptible person, a rotter or cad.

clue.text: Area of New Zealand not initially hosting new dance

indicators.note: a host takes a guest in, so one piece goes inside another
not initially means without the first letter

parts.note: Otago is a region in the South Island of New Zealand
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A New Zealand region is not the first place to stage a fresh dance.
explanation.walkthrough: OTAGO drops its O to give TAGO, which takes in N.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina, performed by couples with sharp, dramatic steps.

clue.text: Rest before quick meal

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the next

parts.note: a break is a rest
fast means quick

explanation.surface: Take a pause before grabbing a hurried bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick meal' reads as one phrase, but 'quick' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast is the first eating occasion of the day, taken in the morning.

clue.text: Artist joining the writer and family for a small dish

indicators.note: joining puts things side by side, so the pieces follow on

parts.note: an RA is a Royal Academician
the writer refers to the setter, me
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: An artist comes over to share a little plate with the setter and relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, ME and KIN run together in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramekin is a small ceramic bowl used for baking and serving individual portions.

clue.text: Novice's first use of firearms not good in religious establishment

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the opening letter of novice

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: gunnery is the operation of guns
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A novice handling guns for the first time is out of place in a convent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novice' suits the convent scene, as a novice nun, but only its first letter is used; the firearms word then loses its good.
explanation.definitionFit: A nunnery is a convent, a house where a community of nuns lives under religious vows.
